New York wants to curb temporary health care workers by capping staffing agencies’ profits. But price controls don’t create workers—they reduce supply and flexibility, especially for rural & underserved hospitals. The result could be worse shortages and higher costs.

ow.ly/VgJV50YLnow

Birthright citizenship is back at the Supreme Court—and the debate keeps reaching for 19th‑century anti‑Asian cases. Cato’s Peter VanDoren revisits how officials and unions once tried to “stamp out” Chinese restaurants as a “menace to society.” 
ow.ly/n4Xa50YLlKE

Immigrants generate 17% more in taxes per capita than the US-born person, Cato’s @David_J_Bier reports. 

The primary reason that immigrants pay more in taxes than the average person is that they are far more likely to be employed than the average person.  

ow.ly/3oVz50YKHqu

David Boaz, Cato’s longtime executive vice president and author of The Libertarian Mind, helped define a generation’s understanding of the relationship between government power and human flourishing. His words remain as relevant as ever.

What if “school” started with an hour of play outside? 

Former public school teacher Ashley Wagner built Petrichor School—a Nebraska microschool rooted in movement, hands-on projects, and imagination. A fresh take on learning. 

Read more: ow.ly/7UK650YLoHG

Australia’s social media ban for minors isn’t working: 61% of kids still access accounts, while 4.7M were shut down. Meanwhile, 27% moved to riskier platforms. The ban isn't helping kids— it is harming them. Parents, not the government, are better suited to manage kids’ online use, says Cato's @dr_inserra.

Learn more: ow.ly/6cM250YLfRN

Consumer prices are up 28% in six years and inflation is accelerating again. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @MrRBourne, @JaiKedia, @cpgrabow, and @sslivinski unpack Cato’s new Handbook on Affordability and the macroeconomic and supply-side reforms that could actually help. 
 
Spotify: ow.ly/JNq650YLlqB 
Apple: ow.ly/zS3y50YLlqK  
Our website: ow.ly/oL5l50YLlqP

DOJ lawyers must serve the Constitution, not the President. Cato's Dan Greenberg argues that Pam Bondi repeatedly flouted legal norms as AG. She engineered partisan loyalty tests for career attorneys, groundless prosecutions of Trump's political enemies, and attempts to shield her own office from ethics rules.

Read more: ow.ly/WEum50YLfqb

Former President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump both offered relief when Obamacare made coverage unaffordable and rationed care. Congress should make the relief they pioneered universal and permanent, argues Cato’s @mfcannon. On April 17, he presented a potentially bipartisan blueprint on Capitol Hill.

FISA Section 702 isn't just a surveillance issue — it's a Second Amendment issue. American competitive shooters, gun dealers, and firearms importers could have their data swept into warrantlessly searchable government databases. Cato's @PGEddington explains. 
ow.ly/gIwg50YLkBh

Jeanine Pirro touts strong Second Amendment credentials—but her office’s court filings tell a different story. By supporting DC’s bid to rehear a ruling that struck down the city’s 10‑round magazine limit, prosecutors want to narrow gun rights even while praising them in public. 

Read More: ow.ly/ZoEn50YLeVw

The notion that Washington actively supported Iranian self-determination contradicts the historical record of US Middle East policy—including in Iran. Jon Hoffman argues as the costs of the Iran war become more evident, so too will the chasm between reality and the rhetoric used to justify it. ow.ly/lqop50YLcWE

Greed didn’t cause the recent inflation. The real drivers were Fed-enabled money creation and too much government spending.

Americans are struggling with high prices and high interest rates. Affordability is Washington's defining issue of 2026 and a political headache for both parties. 

The Cato Institute “Handbook on Affordability” features 100+ policy ideas to defuse inflation and lower the cost of living: ow.ly/tRpw50YLbfx

The Constitution gives Congress, not the president, the power to decide when America goes to war. America's founders designed it that way deliberately—and it’s time for legislators to reassert that power, argues Cato’s @Doug_Bandow.

ow.ly/RihH50YKENT

Immigrants generate more income and taxes than the average US-born person, Cato’s @David_J_Bier reports. 
  
From 1994 to 2023, immigrants generated roughly $100,000 more in taxes per capita than the average US-born person—about 17% more over the entire period. 

ow.ly/pFek50YKFMx

A federal appeals court struck down the 150-year-old ban on home distilling, ruling Congress can't use the tax power as a tool of prohibition. This is a win for hobbyists—and for the principle that federal power has constitutional limits.  

Learn more: ow.ly/mO3r50YK8bS

Under the Trump administration the number of refugees who enter legally and are granted full protection based on their fears of persecution has declined by nearly 90%, reports Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

ow.ly/9x7H50YK2RB

Americans are angry about affordability, and policymakers face mounting pressure to “do something." 

Cato’s “Handbook on Affordability” offers 100+ practical policy ideas to improve monetary and fiscal policy — and lower prices by opening up supply and competition in food, energy, housing, healthcare, and more.
